grh_0b873c23070994a3bb35.title: The Shipboard Jewel Robbery
paragraphs: Working as a steward aboard a luxury liner, Rocky gets caught in the theft of Lady Harkness’s jewels and is framed for the murder of ship’s doctor Harper. The jewels had been mixed into the plaster cast on Rocky’s injured arm so they could pass through a shipwide search, but the doctor’s plan to X-ray the cast threatened to expose them. Rocky identifies nurse Helen and her partner Larry as the thieves, with Helen also responsible for killing Harper, and the captain overhears enough of her confession to clear Rocky and recover the jewels.

Love as director, George Lefferts as writer, and Edward King as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Rocky Fortune]].

grh_0b7d6d5c31f7a46d3190.title: Incident at Shadow Valley
paragraphs: At a lonely roadside diner, owner Pop worries about his dangerously ill grandson while police search for a black truck that forced another vehicle off the road. A strange driver named Janus arrives, talks coldly about death and seems to bring fear wherever he goes. Pop finally pulls a gun and forces Janus to drive west, after which the boy suddenly begins improving. Police soon report that no such truck passed them in either direction. Pop concludes that he has faced the Angel of Death itself and, by driving the visitor away, won his grandson another chance to live.

grh_0b40c62d36f17b33e223.title: Glamour
paragraphs: Thirteen years earlier, young widow Ellen McCarty asked Dr. Christian to find a home for her three-year-old daughter Glamour because Ellen intended to marry wealthy Carter Gaylord, who did not know the child existed. John and Evie Clark raised Glamour with Ellen's financial support. After Gaylord's death, Ellen returns to Rivers End and seeks custody of the now sixteen-year-old girl, promising wealth, travel and every social advantage. A judge leaves the final choice to Glamour. When Christian refuses to influence her, Ellen tries to force the decision by offering lifelong security to the Clarks if Glamour comes with her and threatening to withdraw every cent if she refuses. Glamour angrily chooses John and Evie and rejects the mother who abandoned her. The confrontation brings on another heart attack for Evie, and Ellen finally begins to understand that money and pressure cannot manufacture affection. Christian tells her that if she truly wants her daughter back in her life she must earn that relationship through patience and consideration. He suggests that Ellen build a summer cottage nearby, giving mother and daughter a chance to know each other gradually without uprooting Glamour from the family that raised her.
This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on April 17, 1940. It is listed as episode 76 in the archive.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes.
